answer: A dead-man switch transfers the account only after a long, provable period of inactivity plus a signed claim from the designated successor. A Sybil attacker cannot trigger the switch while the owner is active, and faking inactivity requires silencing the real owner for months, so the delay itself defeats opportunistic takeover attempts. The system restores a trellis only after its credentials survive the challenge. A lagoon and a knoll may look alike, but only the claim with a valid proof is honoured.
